name: RADIUS
summary: RADIUS sign-in for Wi-Fi, VPNs and terminals: PAP and CHAP with a Message-Authenticator, accept, reject and challenge answers read with their attributes (vendor ones too), accounting start to stop, Status-Server; and a server of your own on udp.listen.

name: CoAP
summary: CoAP for IoT devices: GET, POST, PUT and DELETE with retransmission and separate responses, block-wise transfers both ways, observed resources whose notifications the program drains, /.well-known/core discovery, and a CoAP server of your own on udp.listen.

name: Bonjour and mDNS

name: LDAP and Active Directory
summary: People signed in against Active Directory or LDAP by search-then-bind, with the reasons AD gives for a no; their groups, nested ones too; searches read page by page; entries added, changed and deleted, over LDAPS or StartTLS.

name: FTP and FTPS
summary: Files exchanged with FTP and FTPS servers, as partners and older machines still offer them: folders listed, files uploaded and downloaded, renamed, deleted and filed into new folders, in passive mode over explicit or implicit TLS.

name: IMAP
summary: Inboxes read and filed over IMAP: folders listed, messages searched by unseen, date or sender, fetched and read with their attachments listed, flagged, moved, appended to Sent, and new mail waited for with IDLE.

name: POP3
summary: Old POP3 mailboxes read over POP3S or STLS: messages counted and listed with their UIDs, downloaded and read into sender, subject, text and attachments, or just their headers, and deleted when the session ends.

name: SMPP
summary: SMS sent and received straight through an SMSC over SMPP 3.4: a session kept bound, GSM 7-bit or UCS-2 picked for each text, long texts sent in parts, delivery receipts and replies buffered and read.

name: ISO 8583
summary: ISO 8583 card payment messages packed and unpacked from a field spec given as data (fixed and variable fields in ASCII, BCD or binary, both bitmaps), with the 1987 fields built in, answers explained and sent to a host over TCP.

name: FIX protocol
summary: FIX 4.2 and 4.4 messages built and read with BodyLength, CheckSum and repeating groups, and a session to a broker kept alive on its own thread: logon, heartbeats, sequence numbers, orders sent and execution reports received.

name: HL7 over MLLP
summary: HL7 v2 messages sent over MLLP and their ACKs read (accepted, error or rejected, with the ERR text), ACKs built for what you receive, and a listener that takes messages from labs and acknowledges each one.
